questions.question: Which one of the following is the overflow condition if linear queue is implemented using an array with a size MAX_SIZE?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: With 0-based indexing the last valid index is MAX_SIZE - 1, so the queue is full (overflow) when rear = MAX_SIZE - 1. rear = MAX_SIZE is already out of bounds.

questions.question: The SQL keyword ________ is used with wildcards.
questions.explanation: The LIKE operator is used with the wildcards % and _ for pattern matching. IN and NOT IN test membership in a list and DISTINCT removes duplicates.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a constructor in OOP?

options.B: To create instances of abstract classes

questions.explanation: A constructor runs automatically when an object is created and initializes its data members. Destroying objects is the job of a destructor.

questions.question: Which of the following is a divide-and-conquer algorithm?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Merge sort divides the array into halves, sorts them recursively and merges them, which is divide and conquer. Heap sort and bubble sort are not.

questions.question: Computer is free from tiredness and boredom. We call it
questions.explanation: Diligence means a computer can work for long hours without tiredness, boredom or loss of concentration. Reliability refers to consistent correct results.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the level of data abstraction that describes exactly how the data is stored?
questions.explanation: The physical level is the lowest level of abstraction and describes how data is actually stored. The conceptual/logical level describes what data is stored and its relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following conversion is not possible (algorithmically)?

options.B: Non-deterministic pushdown automata to deterministic pushdown automata
options.C: Non-deterministic finite state automata to deterministic finite state automata
options.D: Non deterministic Turing machine to deterministic Turing machine

questions.explanation: NPDAs accept all context-free languages but DPDAs accept only deterministic CFLs, so there is no general NPDA to DPDA conversion. NFA to DFA (subset construction) and NTM to DTM conversions always exist.

questions.question: About IoT, which among the following is not correct?

options.D: Push button is a digital Sensor

questions.explanation: A microphone produces a continuously varying voltage, so it is an analog sensor; the statement calling it digital is incorrect. A light sensor (LDR) is analog, while keyboards and push buttons give discrete on/off signals.

questions.question: Which form of e-marketplace brings together buyers and sellers from multiple industries, often for MRO materials?
questions.explanation: A horizontal e-marketplace serves buyers and sellers across many industries, typically for common MRO supplies. A vertical marketplace focuses on a single industry.

questions.question: What is the purpose of ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)?

options.A: To assign IP addresses to devices
options.B: To resolve domain names to IP addresses
options.C: To map MAC addresses to IP addresses

questions.explanation: ARP maps (resolves) between IP and MAC addresses: given a known IP address it finds the corresponding MAC address on the LAN. Resolving domain names is DNS and assigning IPs is DHCP.

questions.question: Which principle ensures that only essential information is visible to the outside world?
questions.explanation: The information hiding principle states that a module exposes only what others need (its interface) and hides its internal details. Encapsulation is the mechanism (bundling data with methods) and abstraction is about modelling essential features, so they are close but the principle named for restricting visibility is information hiding.

questions.question: Slide sorter can be accessed from which menu?
questions.explanation: Slide Sorter is a view, so it is accessed from the View menu (View > Slide Sorter).

questions.question: Context switching in an operating system refers to the process of:

options.A: Switching between user and kernel modes
options.B: Switching between processes to allow multitasking

questions.explanation: A context switch saves the state (PCB) of the running process and loads that of another so the CPU can be shared among processes. A user-to-kernel mode switch is a mode switch, not a context switch.

questions.question: Even with two-factor authentication, users may still be vulnerable to _____ attacks.
questions.explanation: A man-in-the-middle (e.g. real-time phishing proxy) attacker can intercept both the password and the one-time code or the session cookie, so 2FA alone does not stop it. The other options are not standard attack names in this context.

questions.question: The default value for the type attribute of an Unordered List in HTML is:
questions.explanation: The default type (bullet) for an HTML unordered list is a filled disc. Circle and square must be set explicitly; triangle is not a valid type.

questions.question: What is the term for defining multiple methods in a class with the same name but different parameters?
questions.explanation: Overloading means several methods share a name but differ in parameter lists. Overriding redefines an inherited method with the same signature.

questions.question: The concept of monitors was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Among the options, Edsger Dijkstra is credited with the early idea of monitors (formalized later by Hoare and Brinch Hansen); he also introduced semaphores. Turing, Berners-Lee and Torvalds are known for computability, the WWW and Linux respectively.

questions.question: How can we describe an array in the best possible way?

options.B: Container that stores the elements of similar types
options.C: The array is not a data structure
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An array is a data structure that stores elements of the same (similar) type in contiguous locations. Arrays are mutable and are a data structure.

questions.question: Let u = '1101', v = '0001', then uv = 11010001 and vu = 00011101. Using the given information, what is the identity element for the string?
questions.explanation: Concatenation is not commutative (uv differs from vu), and its identity element is the empty string ε since εw = wε = w. Strings have no inverses like u^-1.

questions.question: Which wireless communication technology is commonly used in IoT devices for short-range communication?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bluetooth (especially BLE) is the standard low-power, short-range technology for IoT devices. 4G LTE is a long-range cellular technology.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for sending emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email. HTTP is for web pages, FTP for file transfer and SNMP for network management.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of DBMS?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Common DBMS types are hierarchical, network, relational and object-oriented. Sequential refers to file organization, not a DBMS type.

questions.question: "Ctrl + Left Arrow" is used to

options.A: move the cursor at the beginning of the line
options.B: move the cursor one word left
options.C: move the cursor one paragraph up
options.D: move the cursor one paragraph down

questions.explanation: Ctrl+Left Arrow moves the cursor one word to the left. Home moves to the beginning of the line and Ctrl+Up moves one paragraph up.

questions.question: Which of the following is a technique that marks the beginning of computer communications?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Time sharing, where many users shared one computer through remote terminals, marked the beginning of computer communications. Batch processing involved no interactive communication with users.

questions.question:
Consider the statements given below and then choose the correct output from the given options:
L = ['TIC', 'TAC']
print(L[::-1])
questions.explanation: L[::-1] reverses the order of the list elements, not the characters of each string, giving ['TAC', 'TIC']. Option C reverses each string as well.
